issues.title: BUG: np.unwrap accumulates rounding errors
issues.body:
### Describe the issue:

When used with large values and on large arrays, the values towards the end of the array can have very large errors in phase. This is because the implementation calculates corrections to the differences between elements, then applies np.cumsum to it to determine the corrections to the elements. Since every term has rounding error, the tail of the cumsum has a large error.

This could be improved by calculating corrections in units of the period, which would be integral and hence only suffer from overflow when large enough not to fit into the floating-point type (2^53 for float64).

### Reproduce the code example:

```python
import numpy as np

tau = 2 * np.pi

def phase_error(x, y):
    return (x - y + np.pi) % tau - np.pi

x = np.random.uniform(-1e9, 1e9, size=64 * 1024 * 1024)
y = np.unwrap(x)
print("Max phase error for np.unwrap: ", np.max(np.abs(phase_error(x, y))))
# This gives more accurate results
z = np.unwrap(x / tau, period=1.0) * tau
print("Max phase error for adjusted np.unwrap: ", np.max(np.abs(phase_error(x, z))))
```


### Error message:

```shell
Max phase error for adjusted np.unwrap:  3.597418789524909e-07
```

comments.body:
@bmerry Alternatively, one could rewrite this function such that it doesn't cumsum over non-integral arrays. I wrote such an implementation, and it does in fact get more accurate results (without the external division you did). The runtime is approximately the same as the original implementation (and even a little bit faster).
If time permits I will write a PR to commit this in soon.

```python
import numpy as np

def my_unwrap(p, discont=None, axis=-1, period=2*np.pi):
    p = np.asarray(p)
    dd = np.diff(p, axis=axis)
    dtype = np.result_type(dd, period)
    
    if np.issubdtype(dtype, np.integer):
        half_period, rem = np.divmod(period, 2)
        boundary_ambiguous = rem == 0
    else:
        half_period = period / 2
        boundary_ambiguous = True

    dd_mod_2period = np.mod(dd, 2 * period)
    dd_periods = np.round(dd / period).astype(int)

    if boundary_ambiguous:
        neg_corrections = (dd_mod_2period == half_period + period) & (dd > 0)
        pos_corrections = (dd_mod_2period == half_period) & (dd < 0)
        dd_periods[neg_corrections] -= 1
        dd_periods[pos_corrections] += 1

    if discont is not None and discont > half_period:
        dd_periods[np.abs(dd) < discont] = 0

    phase_shifts = np.cumsum(dd_periods, axis=axis)

    slices = [slice(None)] * p.ndim
    slices[axis] = slice(1, None)
    indices = tuple(slices)
    p_unwrapped = p.copy()
    p_unwrapped[indices] -= phase_shifts * period

    return p_unwrapped
```


comments.body:
The problem is how we should handle objects that are integer like (are currently converted to integers), but are _not_ proper Python integers in light of (NEP 50)[https://numpy.org/neps/nep-0050-scalar-promotion.html].

On NumPy 1.26 this didn't matter, because even using a NumPy `np.int64()` would not have raised the error here even though it _should_ as it is "strongly typed" and you cannot mix unsigned ints and `int64` with `bitwise_or` (it is unclear which type the result should be.  NumPy tends to guess at `float64` which is weird, but doesn't work for bitwise operations).

The choice is currently to only weakly type Python integers, because the main intention is to special case code like `arr + 1` i.e. with a literal.
That effectively is a decision to not special case `IntEnum` (for simplicity also).  But that means it behaves the same as `np.array(value)`.

Now `IntEnum` is an integer subclass (IIRC), so it sits in a somewhat special place:
* On the one hand: We could just make it work the same as a Python integer.
* On the other hand: There is no guarantee that the integer subclass _should_ actually behave exactly the same as a Python integer.

I think @ChrisS85 and @bauergeorg are experiencing https://github.com/mesonbuild/meson/issues/13841, which is a bug in older versions of meson: it is fixed in meson 1.6.1 and up, but they are using 1.5.2 which is too old to contain that bug fix.

There is not enough information here to tell whether the original reporter @JamesonNetworks was experiencing the same thing (because they didn't copypaste the Meson version in use), but I suspect that they were.

There is not enough information here to tell whether @nebhead is experiencing the same thing. "it basically hangs" sounds like a different symptom, which should maybe be reported separately with full details.

> It also doesn't quite make sense that the build log says Build type: native build but the error message is for a cross build.

Yes, that didn't make sense. It was a Meson bug: different parts of Meson had a different idea of whether they were doing a cross or native build.
